issues.status: Archived from the previous Chinese daily digest and translated into English for presentation.
highlights: OpenAI was pushing ChatGPT from an individual tool into household, caregiver and senior-user scenarios.
Meta removed an Instagram AI image feature after backlash over consent and misuse risks.
Apple sued OpenAI over alleged trade-secret issues, potentially affecting OpenAI’s hardware ambitions.
Generative AI capital expenditure remained a major investor concern.
Copyright and training-data litigation continued to pressure AI companies’ data governance.

stories.title: OpenAI advances GPT-5.6 and workplace products
stories.summary: The archived brief reported OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 family, including Sol, Terra and Luna variants, aimed at enterprise, coding and scientific workflows. It also referenced ChatGPT Work as part of a broader productivity push.
stories.whyItMatters: The model race was shifting from raw capability toward cheaper, faster and workflow-specific deployment.

stories.title: Meta enters the AI coding race with Muse Spark 1.1
stories.summary: Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1 was described as a multimodal agentic coding model for multi-step reasoning, tool use and enterprise workflows. Its reported pricing strategy targeted lower-cost enterprise usage.
stories.whyItMatters: Coding assistants became one of the most important commercialization fronts for frontier models.

stories.title: OpenAI targets family, caregiver and senior-user experiences
stories.summary: The brief noted OpenAI hiring for product leadership focused on families, caregivers and older users. The likely product direction included household plans, child profiles, parental controls and care reminders.
stories.whyItMatters: Consumer AI safety requirements become stricter when products move into family and child-facing environments.

stories.title: Meta removes controversial Instagram AI image feature
stories.summary: Meta removed an Instagram feature that let users generate or alter images using public-account photos without automatically notifying the referenced person. The feature was withdrawn after backlash from users and representatives.
stories.whyItMatters: AI image features must handle consent, likeness rights, harassment and deepfake risks before scale.

stories.title: NYT accuses OpenAI of hiding evidence in copyright case; OpenAI denies it
stories.summary: The New York Times and Daily News accused OpenAI of insufficient disclosure related to training data and chat-log search capabilities. OpenAI denied the allegations and argued the plaintiffs sought unrelated private user conversations.
stories.whyItMatters: Copyright cases increasingly focus on what AI companies store, search and disclose, not only whether training qualifies as fair use.

discordShort: OpenAI moved GPT-5.6 and ChatGPT Work further into enterprise workflows.
Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1 entered the crowded AI coding market.
OpenAI showed interest in family and caregiver product experiences.
Meta pulled an Instagram AI image feature after consent concerns.
NYT vs OpenAI highlighted copyright, evidence and user-privacy tensions.
